# Vehicle wraps

## Vehicle Wraps in Vaughan & Toronto
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/vehicle-wraps/

Full and partial vehicle wraps in Vaughan, serving Toronto & the GTA. Commercial, fleet and colour-change wraps with a 5-year workmanship warranty.

Commercial fleet graphics, full colour-change wraps and paint protection film — designed, printed and installed in-house.

Satin Graphic (Satin Auto Wrap) designs, prints and installs vehicle wraps in its own shop at 50 Viceroy Rd in Vaughan, Ontario, for businesses and drivers across Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area. We do commercial and fleet wraps, vehicle lettering and decals, colour-change wraps and paint protection film (PPF).

### Questions
**How long does a van wrap last?**
With cast film and laminate, expect 5–7 years on vertical panels in Ontario weather. Horizontal surfaces (hood and roof) see more sun and typically run 3–5 years. Our workmanship warranty covers lifting and peeling for 5 years.

**Will the wrap damage the paint?**
No — on factory OEM paint the film removes cleanly and actually protects the finish underneath. Repainted or damaged panels can lift with the wrap, which we flag during the inspection before we quote.

**Can I wrap only part of the vehicle?**
Yes. Decals and lettering, a partial wrap, a half / ¾ wrap and a full wrap are all priced separately — the coverage cards above show the split. Partial wraps are designed so the vehicle’s own colour becomes part of the layout.

**Do you handle the design?**
We do. Our in-house team builds the layout on your vehicle’s template for a $250 design deposit that’s credited to the wrap when you proceed. If you already have artwork, send it and we’ll proof it at scale.

**How do I look after it?**
Hand wash with a mild automotive soap, keep pressure washers at least 60 cm from edges, and skip wax on matte or satin finishes. We send a care sheet with every install.

**What about multiple vehicles?**
Fleet pricing kicks in at three or more vehicles and includes a brand template so every new vehicle you add matches the last one exactly.

**Do you wrap the roof of a van?**
Rarely — it’s not visible from the street, so most fleet wraps stop at the roofline. If your vans park under office windows or in a downtown core, a roof panel with your logo is a cheap add-on.

## Vehicle Lettering & Decals in Vaughan & GTA
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/vehicle-wraps/lettering/

Vehicle lettering, truck decals and van graphics in Vaughan for Toronto & GTA businesses. Designed, printed and installed in-house, about 22% of a full-wrap…

Satin Graphic (Satin Auto Wrap) designs, prints and installs vehicle lettering, truck decals and van graphics at its shop in Vaughan, Ontario. Lettering is the most affordable way to put your business on the road: it typically costs about 22% of a full printed wrap for the same vehicle, and it can be upgraded to a partial or full wrap later.
- Typical price: About 22% of a full wrap · full wraps from $2,800 (car) / $3,950 (Transit van)
- Where: 50 Viceroy Rd, Unit 22–23, Vaughan — serving Toronto and the GTA
- What we letter: Vans, pickups, box trucks, trailers, buses, cars and fleets
- Design: In-house, laid out on your exact vehicle template

### Questions
**How much does vehicle lettering cost?**
Lettering and decals usually cost about 22% of a full printed wrap for the same vehicle. For reference, full wraps start at $2,800 for a car and $3,950 for a Transit-size van, before tax. Send a photo of the vehicle and your logo for an exact price.

**What can you put on a work vehicle?**
Your company name, logo, phone number, website and list of services on the doors, sides and rear, plus unit numbers. Perforated window film can carry graphics over rear and side glass.

**Is lettering cheaper than a wrap?**
Yes. Lettering and decals use less film and less installation time than a partial (about 45% of the full-wrap price), ¾ (about 70%) or full wrap.

**Will decals damage my paint?**
No. Quality cast vinyl removes cleanly from factory (OEM) paint when it is taken off properly.

**Do you letter trucks, trailers and fleets?**
Yes — vans, pickups, box trucks, trailers, buses and multi-vehicle fleets. Fleet pricing starts at 3 vehicles and every vehicle gets the same layout.

**Do you design the lettering?**
Yes. Our in-house designers lay it out on your exact vehicle template so text never lands on a door handle or panel gap. You can also send print-ready artwork.

## Colour Change Car Wraps in Vaughan & Toronto
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/vehicle-wraps/color-change/

Colour change car wraps in Vaughan & Toronto in gloss, satin, matte and colour-shift films. Protects factory paint and removes cleanly. Get a quote.

Premium finishes for a completely new look — fully reversible, and easier on resale value than paint.

A colour-change wrap replaces the visible colour of your car with cast vinyl film — gloss, satin, matte, satin chrome or colour-flip — without repainting. It protects the factory paint underneath and comes off cleanly from OEM paint when you want the original colour back.

### Questions
**Does a colour-change wrap hurt resale value?**
The opposite, usually — the film has been protecting the original paint, and it comes off cleanly on OEM finishes. Many owners remove it before sale to reveal a like-new finish.

**How long does the colour last?**
Gloss films run 5–7 years; matte and satin 3–5 years; chrome and colour-flip 2–3 years on horizontal surfaces. All of them longer if the vehicle is garaged.

**Can you match a specific paint colour?**
We can get close with the standard ranges, and printed colour-change film lets us hit an exact swatch when a close match isn’t enough.

**Are door jambs included?**
Not by default. Most customers skip them; if you want a full match with the doors open, add jambs and we’ll quote the extra labour.

**Can I take it through a car wash?**
Touchless washes are fine. Brush washes will eventually scuff the film, especially matte and satin — hand washing is best.


## Car Wrap Visualizer – Preview 3M & Avery Colours
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/vehicle-wraps/visualizer/

Try 200+ 3M, Avery Dennison, KPMF and ORACAL wrap colours on your type of vehicle. Choose finish, window tint and wheels, then get a custom quote in Vaughan.

Upload a photo of your own car or pick a popular model, then preview hundreds of 3M, Avery Dennison, KPMF and ORACAL colour-change films with real reflections and shading. Compare before and after, then send the build to us for a custom quote.

Choose your type of vehicle, then browse colour-change films from 3M, Avery Dennison, KPMF and ORACAL by colour and finish — gloss, satin, matte, metallic and colour-shift. Add a window tint shade and a wheel colour to see the whole look, and send the build to us for a quote.

### Questions
**Are the colours on screen accurate?**
They are a close guide, but every screen shows colour differently and metallic or colour-shift films change with the light. Compare physical samples at the shop before you commit.

**How do I get a quote for the colour I picked?**
When you are happy with the build, send it to us from the visualizer with your vehicle details. We reply with a quote for the film and coverage you chose, usually within one business day.


## Paint Protection Film (PPF) in Vaughan
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/vehicle-wraps/paint-protection-film/

Paint protection film (PPF) in Vaughan: clear, self-healing film for partial front, full front or full body. Stops stone chips and road salt.

Self-healing film for high-impact areas or the entire vehicle — invisible until it saves your paint.

Every painted panel covered in self-healing film that shrugs off light swirl marks with heat.

### Questions
**Can you see the film?**
On a properly installed job, no — the edges are wrapped around panel edges and the film is optically clear. A close look at the hood may show a faint edge line on partial-front packages, which is why many customers choose full-hood coverage.

**How long does PPF last?**
XPEL Ultimate Plus carries a 10-year manufacturer warranty against yellowing, cracking and delamination. Most installs outlast that.

**Does it yellow?**
Older films did. Modern urethane films with a UV-stable top coat don’t yellow within their warranty period.

**PPF or ceramic coating?**
They do different jobs. Ceramic coating makes washing easier and adds gloss but doesn’t stop rock chips. PPF stops chips. The best result is PPF on the front with ceramic over everything.

**Can I get PPF over a wrap?**
Yes, on a fresh wrap — it’s a common combination for matte colour changes that need protection from stains.


## Vehicle Wrap Cost Estimator (Ontario)
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/vehicle-wraps/estimator/

Estimate your vehicle wrap cost in under a minute: cars, SUVs, pickups, vans, box trucks, trailers and buses, priced by our Vaughan wrap shop.

Explore your vehicle category, then choose its size, wrap coverage, material and finish for a tailored estimate.

Each category starts from the square footage of film that vehicle class needs, then scales it by coverage (decals through full wrap), material and finish. The vehicle-specific questions on each page — roof height, cab size, box length — are exactly what moves the real quote.

### Questions
**How accurate is the online estimate?**
Usually within 10–15% of the final quote. The vehicle-specific questions on this page (roof height, cab size, box length) are exactly what drives the film count, so answer them as best you can.

**Does the price include design?**
Basic layout of supplied artwork is included. Fully custom design is a $250 deposit that comes off the wrap price when you go ahead.

**Why does the finish change the price?**
Matte, satin and especially chrome / colour-flip films cost more per metre and take longer to install cleanly. Gloss is the baseline.

**Can I get a firm quote without visiting?**
Send us photos of all four sides and a clear shot of any damage. For most vehicles that’s enough to firm the number up; we confirm on drop-off.

**How long will my vehicle be off the road?**
Sedans and SUVs are usually one day; vans and pickups one to two; box trucks, trailers and buses two to three depending on coverage.


# Window tint, window graphics & walls

## Window Tinting in Vaughan & Toronto
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/window-tint/

Window tinting in Vaughan & Toronto for cars, homes and businesses. Ceramic and carbon films in several shades, with Ontario tint-law guidance.

Ceramic, carbon and dyed film for vehicles and buildings. Drag the slider to see how each VLT% reads on glass.

Satin Graphic installs window film for cars, homes and businesses from its Vaughan shop: ceramic, carbon and dyed films in several shades, computer-cut to your glass, with guidance on what Ontario law allows.

## Car Window Tinting in Vaughan & GTA
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/window-tint/vehicle/

Carbon and ceramic film cut to your exact glass — heat rejection, UV block and privacy, without the purple fade.

Carbon and ceramic film cut to your exact glass — heat rejection, UV block and privacy, without the purple fade.

Window film blocks heat and UV without needing to be dark: a ceramic film at 50% VLT can reject more heat than a cheap dyed film at 5%. We carry dyed, carbon and ceramic tiers, computer-cut to your exact glass so there are no gaps or hand-trimmed edges.

### Questions
**Is it legal?**
In Ontario, nothing may be applied to the windshield below the manufacturer’s AS-1 line, and front side windows must not substantially obscure the interior. Rear windows are unrestricted. We’ll recommend compliant options for your fronts.

**Will it bubble or turn purple?**
Dyed films from years ago did. Modern carbon and ceramic films are colour-stable and carry a lifetime manufacturer warranty against bubbling, peeling and fading.

**How dark should I go?**
For heat, choose the tier (ceramic) not the darkness. For privacy, 20% on rear glass is the common choice. Use the VLT preview on the tint hub to compare.

**Does it affect phone or GPS signal?**
Metallic films can. Carbon and ceramic are non-metallic and have no effect on signal.

**How do I clean it?**
Wait a week, then use a soft cloth and an ammonia-free cleaner. Never scrape the film.


## Commercial Window Film in Vaughan & GTA
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/window-tint/commercial/

Solar and privacy film for storefronts, offices and skylights, measured on site and installed after hours.

Solar and privacy film for storefronts, offices and skylights, measured on site and installed after hours.

Commercial solar film can reject up to 80% of solar heat and 99% of UV, cutting glare on screens and easing the load on your HVAC. Privacy, frosted and security films are available for partitions, ground-floor glass and after-hours protection.

## Window Graphics & Storefront Vinyl in Vaughan
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/window-graphics/

Decals, frosted privacy film and full storefront takeovers — measured, quoted and cut to your exact panes.

Decals, frosted privacy film and full storefront takeovers — measured, quoted and cut to your exact panes.

Digitally printed graphics across every pane — campaigns, seasonal takeovers and full brand environments.

### Questions
**Inside or outside the glass?**
Outside gives the crispest read from the street and is standard for opaque decals and perforated film. Inside (reverse-applied) protects the graphic from weather and vandalism and is what we recommend for frosted film and long-term lettering.

**How long does it last?**
Cast opaque vinyl and frosted film: 5–7 years. Perforated and printed films: 2–3 years outdoors, longer inside.

**Will it come off cleanly?**
Yes, within the film’s rated life. Cheap calendared vinyl left on for a decade is what leaves residue; we use cast films and remove them with heat.

**Can I see it before it’s installed?**
We proof every job on a photo of your actual window, to scale, so you can judge the sightline and the size of the lettering.

**What about landlord approvals?**
Most plazas require a sign permit or landlord sign-off for exterior graphics. We can supply drawings for the application.


## Perforated Window Vinyl in Vaughan & GTA
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/window-graphics/perforated-vinyl/

One-way perforated film prints a full-colour image on the glass while staff and customers still see out.

One-way perforated film prints a full-colour image on the glass while staff and customers still see out.

How one-way works The film is printed on one side and punched with thousands of small holes. From outside the eye reads the print; from inside, the dark backing disappears and you see through.

## Offset Printing in Vaughan & Toronto
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/print-shop/offset/

Thoughtful paper, rich colour and considered finishes. Find the right print for your next introduction.

Thoughtful paper, rich colour and considered finishes. Find the right print for your next introduction.

### Questions
**How fast can I get them?**
Print shop orders are ready in 7–10 business days after proof approval and payment. Need them by a specific date? Tell us when you order and we’ll confirm what’s possible.

**Will the colours match my screen?**
Screens are RGB and backlit; print is CMYK on paper, so bright blues and greens shift a little. Build your file in CMYK and, if a colour is critical, ask for a hard-copy proof or a Pantone match.

**What if I don’t have a print-ready file?**
Send what you have — a logo, a Word document, a photo — and choose the design service option. We’ll lay it out, send a proof and only print once you approve it.

**Can I see a sample before ordering?**
Yes. Drop by the shop to feel the stocks, or we can mail a sample pack of the papers you’re deciding between.

**Do you ship?**
Pickup in Vaughan is free. We ship across Canada by courier; shipping is quoted by weight and shown before you confirm.

**What’s your reprint policy?**
If a job doesn’t match the approved proof — wrong colour, trim, or a defect — we reprint it at no charge. Typos in the approved file are on the proof, so please check it carefully.

## Large Format Printing & Banners in Vaughan
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/print-shop/large-format/

High-impact banners, signs and displays for storefronts, events and everything in between. Large Format Printing & Banners in Vaughan from Satin Graphic,…

For sale, sold, open house and for lease signs for agents and brokerages — coroplast, Alumalite or Alupanel.

Removable 30 mil vehicle magnets for agents, trades and delivery cars — full colour, square corners.

### Questions
**How long will it last outside?**
Vinyl banners and coroplast signs are rated for 2–3 years outdoors. Flags see more wind stress and typically last 6–12 months in constant use. Roll-ups and X-frames are indoor products.

**Can you install it?**
Yes — choose “Installation requested” and we’ll quote hanging, mounting or staking on site across the GTA.

**Is the hardware included?**
Where the configurator says so, yes: grommets on banners, H-stakes with yard signs, the stand with roll-ups, the pole kit with flags and the frame with A-frames. Replacement graphics alone are available for all of them.

**What resolution do I need?**
Far less than you’d think. 100–150 DPI at final size is plenty for a banner read from a metre or more away. A logo as vector will always be sharp at any size.

**Can I order one, or is there a minimum?**
No minimum. One banner, one sign, one flag — pricing scales down at quantity, but single pieces are welcome.

**13 oz or 18 oz?**
13 oz is the standard for most banners. 18 oz is heavier and stiffer — choose it for permanent outdoor installs or anything wider than 8 ft.

## Ceramic Coating Vaughan & Toronto
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/auto-detailing/ceramic-coating/

Ceramic coating in Vaughan with preparation tailored to your paint and vehicle use. Compare coating options and request an assessment before selecting a…

Ceramic coating in Vaughan with preparation tailored to your paint and vehicle use. Compare coating options and request an assessment before selecting a package.

A ceramic coating is a thin, hard layer that bonds to the clear coat. It adds gloss and makes the car easier to wash, because dirt and water release more easily than from bare paint or wax. It does not make paint scratch-proof and it does not stop stone chips — that is the job of paint protection film , and the two are often combined. Our guide to PPF vs ceramic coating explains the difference.

### Questions
**Does ceramic coating prevent scratches?**
Ceramic coating is not a substitute for paint protection film and does not make paint scratch-proof.

**How long will it last?**
Longevity depends on the product, preparation, use and maintenance. Product and coverage details are confirmed in your quote.


## Paint Correction Vaughan & Toronto
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/auto-detailing/paint-correction/

Paint correction in Vaughan for visible swirls and light paint defects. We inspect the finish and agree a realistic polishing scope before starting.

Paint correction in Vaughan for visible swirls and light paint defects. We inspect the finish and agree a realistic polishing scope before starting.

Paint correction levels the clear coat with machine polishing to remove swirl marks, light scratches, haze and dullness that wax and glazes only hide. We inspect the paint under proper lighting first and agree a realistic result before starting, because the outcome depends on the condition and thickness of the existing paint.

### Questions
**Will correction remove deep scratches?**
Deep scratches, chips and paint damage may require refinishing. Correction is scoped to the condition of the existing paint.

## Car Wrap Cost in Toronto (2026 Prices)
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/car-wrap-cost-toronto/

Real 2026 car wrap prices from a Vaughan/Toronto shop: cars from $2,800, SUVs $3,400, vans $3,950, plus what changes the price and how to get an exact quote.

Published starting prices from our own estimator, what moves the number up or down, and how to compare quotes from different GTA shops.

At our shop in Vaughan, a full wrap starts at about $2,800 for a car, $3,400 for an SUV and $3,200 for a pickup truck, before 13% HST. Commercial vans start at $3,950 (Transit-size), and box trucks at $5,800. These are the same starting prices our online estimator uses for customers anywhere in Toronto and the GTA.

### Questions
**Is a wrap cheaper than paint?**
Often, yes — especially compared with a quality full respray that includes door jambs. A wrap is also reversible and protects the factory paint. See our wrap vs paint guide for the full comparison.

**Does the price include HST?**
No. Prices on our site are in CAD before 13% HST.

**How much is a wrap for a Tesla Model 3 or Model Y?**
Use the car (sedan) or SUV starting price as a guide — $2,800 and $3,400 — then the estimator adjusts for size, finish and roof. We template EV camera cut-outs and panel gaps to factory spec.

**Do you need a deposit?**
Online estimates in our shop use a 50% deposit to book the work; we confirm the deposit with your final quote.


## Car Wrap vs Paint: Which Is Better?
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/wrap-vs-paint/

Wrap or repaint? Compare cost, time, durability, resale value and repairs for a car wrap vs a paint job in Ontario, with honest advice on when paint wins.

A side-by-side comparison from a wrap shop — including the cases where we’d tell you to paint instead.

Choose a wrap if you want a new colour or branding that’s reversible, protects the factory paint and is done in days. Choose paint if the existing paint is failing, you want a permanent finish for the life of the vehicle, or you’re restoring a classic.

### Questions
**Does a wrap damage paint?**
Not factory paint in good condition. Quality cast film removes cleanly. Repaints and damaged paint can lift with the film, which we flag before quoting.

**Is a wrap cheaper than a paint job?**
Compared with a quality full respray, usually. Compared with a cheap respray, not always — but a cheap respray isn’t reversible and rarely matches a wrap’s finish.

**Can you wrap a car with rock chips?**
Small chips can be wrapped over but may show through, especially in gloss films. Larger chips or rust should be repaired first.


## How Long Does a Car Wrap Last in Canada?
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/wrap-lifespan-canadian-winter/

Vehicle wrap lifespan in Ontario: 5–7 years for printed cast film on vertical panels, less on hoods and roofs. How salt, snow and car washes affect it…

Realistic lifespans for wraps in Ontario weather, what winter actually does to vinyl, and how to make yours last.

With quality cast film and laminate, a printed commercial wrap typically lasts 5–7 years on vertical panels in Ontario weather and 3–5 years on hoods and roofs . Colour change films vary by finish: gloss about 5–7 years, matte and satin 3–5 years, chrome and colour-flip 2–3 years on horizontal surfaces. A garaged vehicle lasts longer.

### Questions
**Does road salt damage vinyl wraps?**
Salt residue and the grit in slush are abrasive and will dull the surface if left on. Regular rinsing prevents most of it.

**Will my wrap crack in the cold?**
Vinyl is less flexible when very cold, so impacts and scraping do more damage in winter. Normal driving in the cold won’t crack a properly installed cast-film wrap.

**Should I remove my wrap before winter?**
No. A wrap in good condition protects the paint underneath from salt and chips through the winter.

**Can I use a car wash in winter?**
Touchless washes are fine. Avoid brush washes, which scuff film over time.


## PPF vs Ceramic Coating: Which Do You Need?
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/ppf-vs-ceramic-coating/

Paint protection film stops rock chips; ceramic coating makes washing easier and adds gloss. Compare protection, lifespan and GTA prices, and when to…

They’re often sold as alternatives, but they do different jobs. Here’s how to choose — or combine them.

Paint protection film (PPF) is a thick, clear urethane film that physically stops rock chips, bug etching and light scratches, and its top coat self-heals light swirls with heat. Ceramic coating is a thin, hard layer that makes paint glossier and much easier to wash, but it does not stop rock chips and doesn’t make paint scratch-proof. For highway driving in the GTA, the best result is PPF on the front of the vehicle with ceramic coating over everything.

### Questions
**Can you put ceramic coating on PPF?**
Yes — and it’s what we recommend. The coating makes the film easier to clean and adds gloss.

**Does PPF yellow?**
Older films did. Modern urethane films with a UV-stable top coat don’t yellow within their warranty period.

**Is ceramic coating worth it on an old car?**
Only after paint correction. A coating locks in whatever is underneath, including swirls.

**How long does PPF take to install?**
Usually one to two days depending on coverage, plus about 48 hours to cure before washing.


## Window Tint Laws in Ontario (2026 Guide)
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/ontario-window-tint-law/

What Ontario allows on the windshield, front side windows and rear glass, how inspections treat tint on newer vehicles, and how to choose a compliant…

A plain-language summary from a tint shop — with links to the official sources, because the rules and how they’re enforced can change.

This guide is general information, not legal advice. The authoritative sources are the Highway Traffic Act and its regulations on Ontario e-Laws and the Ministry of Transportation at ontario.ca . If you’re unsure, ask us before tinting and check those sources.

### Questions
**Is 35% tint legal on front windows in Ontario?**
The Act doesn’t set a percentage; it prohibits front windows that substantially obscure the interior, which is judged by the officer. For 2017-and-newer vehicles, inspection standards are reported to require about 70% light transmission on the front side windows, so darker film there may fail an inspection. Check current rules before you tint.

**Can I tint my windshield in Ontario?**
Aftermarket tint on the windshield is not allowed except a narrow sun strip at the top of the glass.

**How dark can rear windows be in Ontario?**
The Highway Traffic Act restriction applies to the windshield and front side windows, so rear side windows and back glass can be darker. Keep both outside mirrors working.

**What is the fine for illegal tint in Ontario?**
Tickets under section 73 carry a set fine (commonly reported as $85 plus surcharges), and you may be told to remove the film. Check the current amount with the Ministry of Transportation.

Work out the return on a fleet or van wrap with real GTA prices: cost per year, cost per month, break-even jobs, and how to track the leads your wrapped…

A simple, honest way to estimate whether wrapping your work vehicles pays for itself — using our published prices, not inflated impression counts.

With cast film and laminate, about 5–7 years on vertical panels in Ontario weather and 3–5 years on roofs and hoods.

Yes, from three or more vehicles.

Wraps for business vehicles are generally a business expense, but how they’re treated depends on your situation — ask your accountant.

## How to Design a Business Card: 13 Rules
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/business-card-design-tips/

13 practical rules for a business card people keep: what to include, layout, fonts, colour, paper and print-ready files — from a Vaughan print shop.

A business card is small, so every millimetre has a job. These are the rules we use when we lay out cards for GTA businesses — and the mistakes we see most often on files sent to print.

A business card is usually the first printed piece of a brand that someone holds in their hand, and it is often the one they keep in a wallet, a cardholder or a pile on a desk. It is also the cheapest piece of marketing you will buy: at our shop, 500 regular 14 pt matte cards start at $26 before tax. Because it is so inexpensive, the difference between a card that works and one that gets thrown out comes down almost entirely to design and paper — not budget.

### Questions
**What size is a standard business card in Canada?**
3.5 × 2 inches, the same as the US standard. Build the file at 3.75 × 2.25 inches to include a 0.125-inch bleed on every side.

**What should be on a business card?**
Your name and title, business name and logo, one phone number, one email, your website, the address if customers visit you, and a short line that says what you do. Use the back for services, hours or a QR code.

**What paper thickness is best for business cards?**
Our regular cards are 14 pt matte, which feels solid and is easy to write on. For a more premium feel, choose our 16 pt soft-touch luxury cards.

**Should I put a QR code on my business card?**
If it leads somewhere useful — booking, reviews or a portfolio — yes. Print it at least about 0.75 in square with a quiet margin around it, and test it on the proof.

**How long does business card printing take?**
Standard production at our shop is 7–10 business days after you approve the proof and pay.


## Which Wall Mural Material Should I Choose?
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/wall-mural-wallpaper-materials/

Flat matte or texture, removable or permanent adhesive: how to choose a custom wall mural material, with prices, wall prep and install tips.

Custom wall murals look simple, but the material decides how they look up close, how they clean and whether they come off cleanly later. Here is how to choose.

Choose by three things: the finish you want to see , how long the mural should stay up , and the wall it’s going on . For most homes and offices, a flat matte finish with removable adhesive is the safest choice. Choose a textured finish when you want depth and a tactile, canvas-like surface — especially for photographic and botanical designs — and permanent adhesive for high-traffic commercial walls that will stay for years.

### Questions
**What is the best material for a wall mural?**
For most homes and offices, a flat matte finish with removable adhesive. Choose a textured finish for photographic or botanical designs, and permanent adhesive for high-traffic commercial walls.

**How much does a custom wall mural cost?**
At our shop, Flat Matte is $7 per sq ft and Texture is $10 per sq ft before tax, with optional installation at $3 per sq ft. A 12 × 8 ft wall (96 sq ft) in Flat Matte is about $672 before installation.

**Is removable wallpaper really removable?**
It is designed to remove cleanly from properly cured, primed paint, but no adhesive can guarantee damage-free removal on every painted surface. Test a small piece first.

**How long should I wait after painting before installing a mural?**
Long enough for the paint to cure fully — usually several weeks. Check the paint manufacturer’s guidance.

**Can I use my own photo?**
Yes. Upload it on the custom wallpaper page; 100–150 DPI at final size is ideal, and we check every file before printing.


## 7 Ways to Make Your Local Business Visible
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/make-local-business-visible/

Practical ways for GTA businesses to get noticed: Google profile, window graphics, vehicle lettering, sidewalk and yard signs, print and apparel.

Most local customers find a business in one of two ways: they search for it, or they see it. Here are seven practical ways to be seen more often — and how to make each one count.

Before spending on signage or print, make sure people who see your name can find you. Claim and complete your Google Business Profile : correct category, hours, phone, website, service area and real photos of your work, your team and your storefront or vehicles. Use exactly the same business name, address and phone number on your website, your profile, your vehicles and your printed materials. Consistency helps customers trust what they see, and it avoids the frustration of a wrong number printed on a van.

### Questions
**What is the cheapest way to advertise a local business?**
A complete Google Business Profile costs nothing. After that, the lowest-cost physical options are usually window decals, vehicle lettering, yard signs and business cards — each is a one-time cost that keeps working.

**Do I need a permit for a storefront sign in Vaughan or Toronto?**
Exterior signs often need landlord approval and may need a municipal sign permit; rules differ between municipalities and sign types. Check with your landlord and the city before installing. We can supply drawings for an application.

**Is vehicle lettering worth it for a small business?**
For most service businesses, yes: it costs about 22% of a full wrap and puts your name in front of people every day the vehicle is on the road or parked at a job.

**How do I know which advertising is working?**
Ask every new customer how they found you, and use separate phone numbers, landing pages or promo codes for different channels where you can.


## Vehicle Lettering vs Partial vs Full Wrap
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/vehicle-lettering-vs-partial-vs-full-wrap/

Lettering, partial, ¾ or full wrap? What each covers, real GTA prices for cars, vans, pickups and box trucks, and how to choose for your business.

The four levels of vehicle branding, what each one actually covers, what it costs at our Vaughan shop, and how to pick the right one for your business and budget.

If your vehicle’s paint colour works with your brand and the budget is tight, start with lettering or a partial wrap. If the vehicle is your main advertising, or the paint colour clashes with your brand, a full wrap is usually worth it.

### Questions
**How much does van lettering cost?**
At our shop, lettering and decals on a Transit-size van start at about $870 before HST — about 22% of the $3,950 full-wrap price. The final price depends on size and coverage.

**Is a partial wrap worth it?**
Often, yes. A well-designed partial wrap costs about 45% of a full wrap and, on white, black or silver vehicles, can look nearly as striking from the side and rear.

**What is the difference between a ¾ wrap and a full wrap?**
A ¾ wrap covers most of the body but usually leaves the hood, roof or front end in the original paint. A full wrap covers every painted panel.

**Can I upgrade from lettering to a full wrap later?**
Yes. If the original layout was built on your vehicle template, we can extend the same design into a partial or full wrap.

**Do decals damage paint?**
Not factory paint in good condition. Quality vinyl removes cleanly with heat within its rated life. Repainted or damaged panels can lift with the film.


## Roll-Up Banner & Trade Show Display Guide
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/roll-up-banner-trade-show-guide/

Choosing a roll-up banner or X-frame for trade shows and events: sizes, stands, prices, design that reads across the aisle, and care tips.

A good portable display makes a folding table look like a real booth. Here’s how to choose the right size and stand, design it to be read from across the aisle, and keep it looking good show after show.

Both are indoor products . Wind tips them over and sun and rain shorten their life, so for outdoor events use vinyl banners , flags or an A-frame sign instead.

### Questions
**What size roll-up banner should I get?**
33 × 80 in is the standard and fits most tables and spaces. Choose 47 × 80 in if you have room and want a wider layout or a stronger back wall.

**How much does a roll-up banner cost?**
At our shop, a 33 × 80 in roll-up with a standard stand starts at $148.74 before tax, including printing and the stand. Larger size and premium stand are optional upgrades.

**Can roll-up banners be used outdoors?**
They are designed for indoor use. Wind tips them over easily. For outdoor events, use vinyl banners, flags or A-frame signs.

**How long does it take to print a roll-up banner?**
Most large-format pieces are ready in 2–5 business days after proof approval.

**Can I replace the graphic and keep the stand?**
Yes. Replacement graphics are available for roll-ups and X-frames.


## Yard Signs & Lawn Signs Guide (GTA)
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/yard-signs-lawn-signs-guide/

Coroplast vs poly bag lawn signs: sizes, single or double-sided, H-stakes, design tips, GTA prices and the local sign rules to check first.

Yard signs are one of the cheapest ways to get your name in front of a neighbourhood. Here’s how to choose the right type and size, design one that reads from a moving car, and stay on the right side of local sign rules.

Coroplast is the workhorse: full-colour printing, stiff enough to stay readable in wind, and reusable for job after job. Poly bag signs are the budget option when you need hundreds of identical signs for a short period and a simple one- to three-colour design is enough.

### Questions
**What is the standard yard sign size?**
18 × 24 inches. Choose 24 × 36 inches for corner lots, busier roads or when you need to be read from further away.

**How long do coroplast signs last outside?**
Printed coroplast signs are rated for about 2–3 years outdoors. Most are retired earlier because they get bent or the message changes.

**How much do yard signs cost?**
At our shop, an 18 × 24 in single-sided coroplast sign is $19.99 for one, falling to $11.20 each from 25 signs, before tax. Poly bag lawn signs start around $3.92 each in quantities of 1,000.

**Can I put a sign on the boulevard in front of my business?**
Often not without permission. Boulevards and road allowances are usually public property and are covered by municipal sign by-laws. Check with your city before placing a sign there.

**Should I choose single- or double-sided?**
Double-sided if the sign stands perpendicular to the road so drivers see it from both directions; single-sided if it faces the street flat.


## Storefront Window Graphics: Which Film?
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/storefront-window-graphics-guide/

Cut decals, perforated one-way vinyl, frosted film or full print? Compare storefront window graphics: prices, lifespan, install and permits.

Your windows are the biggest sign you already pay for. Here’s how to choose the right film for each job — advertising, privacy or just your hours on the door — and what it costs.

Prices are before tax, with a $75 minimum per order; professional installation adds $3 per sq ft. For full window graphics we offer regular printed vinyl ($9), clear film ($10) and blackout film with grey adhesive ($12) for back-of-house glass that must be completely opaque.

### Questions
**What is the best window film for storefront advertising?**
Perforated one-way vinyl for full-colour images that you can still see out through, cut vinyl decals for logos and hours, and full printed graphics for short campaigns or opaque coverage.

**Can you see through perforated window film?**
Yes, from inside — the view is slightly darker, like looking through a screen. From outside, people see the printed image. Visibility through it is reduced at night when the inside is brighter.

**How much do storefront window graphics cost?**
At our shop, before tax: cut decals $12 per sq ft, perforated vinyl $9, frosted film $7 and printed window graphics from $9, with a $75 minimum. Installation is $3 per sq ft.

**Do I need a permit for window graphics in Vaughan or Toronto?**
It depends on the municipality, the size and whether the sign is inside or outside the glass. Always check with your landlord and the city before a large install.

**Will window vinyl damage the glass?**
No. Quality films remove cleanly from glass with heat within their rated life.


## DTF vs Vinyl vs Embroidery vs Screen Print
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/guides/custom-apparel-printing-methods/

DTF, heat-transfer vinyl, embroidery or screen print? Compare custom apparel methods on look, durability, minimums and cost for shirts and hats.

The decoration method matters as much as the garment. Here’s how DTF, heat-transfer vinyl, embroidery and screen printing compare — and which one to choose for team shirts, uniforms, merch and hats.

Our apparel shop offers DTF and vinyl heat press on T-shirts, hoodies, sweatshirts and workwear, and embroidery on hats and polos. There’s no minimum order, and orders of more than 20 pieces get 5% off.

### Questions
**What is the difference between DTF and screen printing?**
DTF prints a full-colour transfer digitally and heat-presses it onto the garment, with no set-up per colour and no minimums. Screen printing uses one screen per colour, which is economical for large runs of simple designs but expensive for small or multi-colour orders.

**How long does DTF printing last?**
A quality DTF transfer, properly pressed and washed inside out in cool water, typically lasts many dozens of washes. Hot washes, harsh detergents and high dryer heat shorten its life.

**Is embroidery better than printing?**
For hats, polos, jackets and corporate wear, embroidery looks more premium and lasts longer. For full-colour designs, photos or thin T-shirts, printing is the better choice.

**Is there a minimum order for custom shirts?**
Not at our shop. You can order a single shirt, and orders of more than 20 pieces get 5% off.

**Can I buy DTF transfers to press myself?**
Yes. Order custom DTF transfers by size or as a gang sheet, priced by area.

## Wrap, Tint & Print Warranty
URL: https://satingraphic.ca/satin/warranty/

What we stand behind, for how long, and how to make a claim. Wrap, Tint & Print Warranty from Satin Graphic, Vaughan — serving Toronto & the GTA.

Workmanship warranty: 5 years against lifting, peeling and bubbling caused by installation, on vehicles with OEM paint in good condition. Film and print durability are covered separately by the manufacturer (3M, Avery Dennison or Arlon) — typically 5–7 years vertical and 3–5 years horizontal for printed wraps, and 2–7 years for colour-change films depending on finish.

Not covered: damage from accidents, pressure washers at edges, automatic brush washes, chemicals, or wraps applied over repaint, damaged paint or non-OEM panels we flagged at inspection.

### Questions
**How do I get a quote?**
Use the estimator on any product page, add configured items to the quote cart, or hit “Get a Quote” anywhere on the site. Tell us what you need and we reply within one business day with a firm price.

**Where are you located and what are your hours?**
We are in Vaughan, Ontario, serving the Greater Toronto Area. Monday to Friday 9:00–17:00, Saturday 10:00–15:00, closed Sunday. Shop visits are by appointment so the right person is available.

**Do you offer design services?**
Yes — an in-house team designs wraps, print, apparel, window graphics and websites. Design deposits are credited to production when you go ahead.

**Can I pay online?**
Yes — online checkout is live. Add print, label, sign and apparel products to your cart and pay securely online; we check every file before production. Custom work such as wraps, tint and installations is quoted first.

**Do you ship?**
Pickup in Vaughan is free; we ship print and apparel across Canada by courier and install wraps, tint, glass and wall graphics across the GTA.

**What warranty do you offer?**
Five years on wrap workmanship, ten on PPF film, lifetime on tint film, and reprints for any print job that doesn’t match its approved proof. The full terms are on the Warranty page.

**How long does a van wrap last?**
With cast film and laminate, expect 5–7 years on vertical panels in Ontario weather. Horizontal surfaces (hood and roof) see more sun and typically run 3–5 years. Our workmanship warranty covers lifting and peeling for 5 years.

**Will the wrap damage the paint?**
No — on factory OEM paint the film removes cleanly and actually protects the finish underneath. Repainted or damaged panels can lift with the wrap, which we flag during the inspection before we quote.
